Playbook.name: Change Audit — Windows Privileged Group Membership Changed - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Membership of a privileged group (any *Admins/*Administrators/*Operators, Remote Desktop/Management Users, DnsAdmins, GPO Creator Owners) changed via 4728/4729/4732/4733/4756/4757. Broader than the Tier-0 rule - includes operator and remote-access groups. Triage question: authorised group administration, or unexpected privilege grant/removal?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: These groups confer elevated or remote-access rights; unauthorised membership changes enable escalation, lateral access or persistence.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the privileged-group change is authorised administration or an unexpected grant/removal, and whether the added member then used the access.

Step.name: Reconstruct the group change
Step.Purpose: Capture actor, member, group, add-vs-remove for the change-record comparison.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4728","4729","4732","4733","4756","4757") AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.MemberName, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Add codes 4728/4732/4756; remove codes 4729/4733/4757. Adds to Admins/Remote Desktop Users are the escalation cases. A remove may be an attacker covering tracks or normal offboarding.

Step.name: Did the added member then log on or use privilege
Step.Purpose: Immediate use of new group rights (logon to new hosts, special privileges) turns a paperwork gap into an active incident.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: RDP/interactive logon or 4672 special privileges by the added member right after being added indicates the grant was exercised.

Node.Condition: Actor is not an established group admin, or no change record exists.
INV-02 shows the added member immediately used the new access.
Known admin making the change under an approved ticket.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PGRP-CHANGE, INV-02-PGRP-USE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the ticket; close as false_positive.

Indicators.Item: Added member uses access or is a service/normal account.

SOCAction.Item: Reverse if unauthorised; disable involved accounts; open IR.
Fix the mapping; remove errors; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
